title: Marketplace E2E Onboarding Playbook — Vertical ISV (draft)
content:
Purpose: this doc captures a prescriptive end-to-end onboarding playbook for vertical ISVs (initial focus: fintech + healthcare + customer service bots) who want to list Redwood Inference on cloud marketplaces (AWS Marketplace, Azure Marketplace, GCP Marketplace). Draft / working doc: use as a checklist and copy bank for marketplace tile + trial configuration + compliance intake.

Context / problem: marketplace listings are a high-leverage channel but require cross-functional preflight (security, legal, billing, product, infra). Vertical ISVs bring extra constraints (HIPAA, PCI, data residency). This playbook standardizes the steps and acceptance criteria so launches are repeatable.

Goals and success metrics
- Time-to-live for listing: target 6 business days from intake to published tile (metric for FY26).
- Conversion lift: initial hypothesis +10% MQL->trial for marketplace-born trials vs direct signups.
- Compliance gating rate: reduce back-and-forth security questions by 50% through a structured intake form.
- Launch readiness checklist completion >= 95% before scheduling marketplace submission.

Scope and assumptions
- This playbook covers: asset creation (copy + screenshots), trial SKU configuration, security & compliance intake, technical verification, and post-publish QA and observability hooks.
- Assumes ISV can deploy either Hosted (Redwood API) or Dedicated/Private offering. If customer requires on-prem or air-gap, escalate to eng-private-deployments.

Preflight intake (owner: GTM product manager)
- Intake form fields (collect before human review): company legal name, point of contact (email + phone), target vertical, compliance certs (SOC2/HIPAA/PCI), desired supported regions, billing model (SaaS metered / subscription / BYOL), trial SKU: length and token limit, SSO requirement (SAML/OIDC), required data residency.
- Attachments: signed MSA (if needed), security questionnaire, sample privacy notice, logo (SVG + 512x512 PNG), 3 screenshots (desktop app, dashboard, API docs), short 60s video (optional).

Marketplace asset checklist (owner: Partner Ops)
- Tile title (max 90 chars) — 3 variants (dev-friendly, enterprise, exec headline).
- Short tagline (<= 140 chars) — single-sentence benefit.
- 3 bullet benefit list (developer benefits / scale / cost controls).
- Long description (250-400 chars) — includes supported deployment modes and notable compliance.
- Pricing & trial section: trial length, entitlements, post-trial auto-convert behavior, cancellation & refund notes.
- Legal contact + support SLA summary.
- Required images: logo, banner, screenshots, architecture diagram (optional).
- Tech contact for verification + sandbox account credentials.

Sample copy snippets (iteration-ready, use the tone-of-voice bank)
- Tile title variant A (developer-first): "Redwood Inference — production LLM inference, predictable latency"
- Tile title variant B (enterprise): "High-throughput LLM serving with SLAs & private deployments"
- Short tagline: "Ship LLM features faster with predictable latency, cost controls, and private deployment options."
- 3 bullets (bullet-friendly):
  - "Hosted API for immediate launch; Dedicated capacity for predictable throughput."
  - "Transparent per-token economics and token-level cost breakdowns."
  - "Rollouts, canaries, and automated fallbacks to keep services resilient."
- Long description (example): "Redwood Inference is a developer-first LLM inference platform built for production. Support hosted, dedicated, and private deployments to meet latency, compliance, and cost requirements. Includes model catalog, observability dashboards, and rollout controls for safe releases."
- Privacy/compliance snippet (for marketplace privacy box): "Data processed during inference is ephemeral by default. Customers can enable private deployments and KMS-backed encryption for persistent artifacts. See our security page for details: https://redwood.inference/security"

Trial SKU and entitlements (owner: Finance + Partner Ops)
- Typical trial config (vertical ISV recommended default): 30 days OR 100k inference tokens, whichever comes first.
- Option A (developer trial): no CC required, rate-limited sandbox keys, 5k tokens/day.
- Option B (enterprise POC): CC required, 14-day extended trial with on-request quota increases, dedicated pre-provisioned ephemeral capacity for demos.
- Billing mapping: ensure marketplace SKU maps to internal billing SKU (example: MKP-SKU-REDWOOD-TRIAL -> BILL-SKU-RW-TRIAL).

Technical verification tests (owner: Eng QA / Solutions Eng)
- Functional: verify API key provisioning, example request/response, sample embedding generation, stream support works in sandbox.
- Latency smoke: median token latency <= 200ms in target region for demo model; record sample traces.
- Capacity assertion: if listing promises Dedicated capacity, validate autoscale policy and documented throughput (tokens/sec).
- Security: verify that sandbox does not persist PII, run dependency SCA checks, confirm KMS integration where applicable.
- Signup flow: simulate a purchase flow in the marketplace (trial activation -> key issuance -> first request). Document any manual steps.

Acceptance criteria matrix (must-pass items before submission)
- All required assets uploaded (logo, 3 screenshots, banner) -> yes
- Legal contact and support SLA documented -> yes
- Trial SKU defined and mapped to billing -> yes
- Security questionnaire returned and rated green/amber -> green or amber with mitigation plan
- Demo sandbox credentials created and verified by QA -> yes
- UX copy review by GTM (owner sign-off) -> yes

Post-publish QA and monitoring (owner: Product Ops)
- Smoke test published tile: replicate purchase flow in production marketplace (small test order) and verify provisioning chain.
- Instrument metrics: marketplace-origin attribution tag in analytics, first-touch funnel, trial->paid conversion for marketplace cohorts.
- Monitor error rate and latency for marketplace-origin tokens for first 14 days; set alert if error rate > 2% or 95th p90 latency breaches SLO.

Ops & rollout runbook (short)
- Incident routing: pager (oncall-eng), escalation to Partner Ops (pager), notify GTM PM and legal if billing disputes arise.
- Rollback: unpublish tile if billing integration has major defects; communicate to partner via prewritten template.
- Contact points: Partner Ops (primary), Finance (billing mapping), Eng Solutions (sandbox support).

Launch comms checklist
- Partner press/announcement review (marketing + partner comms).
- Internal announcement (product-updates, sales, support) with how to handle marketplace leads.
- Demo playbook for SDRs: 3 talking points + 2 prescriptive demos (hosted quick-start + dedicated POC).

Open questions / notes to self
- Q: For HIPAA customers via marketplace, do we need a separate Marketplace listing text to highlight BAAs? Who owns BAA documentation? (action: legal to confirm)
- Q: Can we support promo codes for marketplace trials or does marketplace force its own trial mechanics? (action: finance to confirm mapping).
- TODO: generate a second set of tile copy that emphasizes cost-savings for high token volumes (Liam).
- TODO: capture a lightweight architecture diagram for "Dedicated capacity" offering (Diego).

Appendix: helpful links and quick templates
- Quick merchant mapping: example billing SKU mapping template (copy into partner intake form).
- Marketplace QA checklist (concrete tests to run during publish window).

Last thoughts: aim to keep the listing copy pragmatic and machine-readable; marketplaces often truncate long copy—prioritize the key developer value props and explicit compliance signals for vertical buyers. This draft intentionally mixes UX copy + operational checklist so partner onboarding is a single cohesive flow.

-- end of draft playbook --
